## California Designer: Sole Proprietor vs LLC

For a California designer with **$72,000 revenue**, **$18,000 deductible expenses**, and a goal of **under 5 hours/month on admin**, the simplest path is usually **sole proprietor**. An LLC can help with liability separation, but it adds state fees, filings, and extra bookkeeping that often outweigh the admin benefit for a solo freelancer at this income level.

## Tax and Paperwork Comparison for This Income Level

| Factor | Sole Proprietor | California LLC |
|---|---|---|
| Federal tax treatment | Report profit on Schedule C | Usually same by default if single-member; can elect different treatment later |
| California state cost | No separate entity fee | **$800 minimum annual franchise tax**; possible additional LLC fee based on revenue |
| Formation paperwork | None beyond local licenses/DBAs if needed | Articles of Organization, registered agent, operating agreement, state filings |
| Ongoing admin | Low | Higher: annual filings, tax payments, separate records, more compliance |
| Bookkeeping | Simple personal-business separation | Better to keep separate bank account and records; more formal tracking |
| Liability protection | No entity shield | Some liability separation, but only if properly maintained |
| Best fit | Lowest admin, lowest cost | Better if liability protection is a priority and admin is acceptable |

## Practical Cost Impact

With your numbers, estimated taxable business profit before other personal deductions is:

- **Revenue:** $72,000
- **Less business expenses:** $18,000
- **Estimated net business profit:** **$54,000**

What matters practically:

- As a **sole proprietor**, you avoid the California LLC minimum tax and extra filing burden.
- As an **LLC**, you likely add at least **$800/year** in California tax, plus formation and annual compliance work.
- For a designer, the federal self-employment tax and income tax usually remain the same if the LLC is taxed as a disregarded entity, so the LLC often does **not** create major tax savings by itself.

## Which Is Simpler Here

**Recommended for simplicity: sole proprietor.**

Why:
- No entity setup
- Less paperwork
- Fewer deadlines
- Easier bookkeeping
- Better match for a solo designer keeping admin under 5 hours/month

When an LLC may still be worth it:
- You want a clearer liability boundary
- You plan to hire contractors or expand
- You’re comfortable paying extra California compliance costs
- You value the formality more than simplicity
